PAN AMERICAN AIRWAYS COMPANY
GENERAL POST OFFICE BUILDING, THIRD FLOOR
250 NORTH SOOCHOW ROAD
SHANGHAI
Person
Baguio, P. I.
Sept. 6, 1937
Mr. S. W. Morgan,
Pan American Airways,
New York.
Dear Stokeley:
I was so wrong in my predictions as to the present Sino-
Japanese trouble that I feel in self defense an explanation is in
at present going
The actual circumstances to express it in another way, were
somewhat as though Jack Dempsey walked into your office and said
"Morgan get under the desk"
You would first look around for help
and seeing no one, if you had good sense you would get under the
desk. If Dempsey
then proceeded to kick you in the pants you woud
then probably suffer that humiliation as gracefully as possible.
If he
then came around and spit in your face you might or might
not
take it but if indignities were carried far enough you might then
come out from under the desk and sock him if you knew it were the
last act of your life.
That I believe is about the situation.
The Chinese, who are extremely proud, suffered every humiliatior
at the hands of the Japanese until finally they could stand no
more and I personally do not believe that any of the responsible
Chinese leaders at any time dared hope for victory.
I personally thought that Chiang Kai-shek would trade it
out with the Japs, agree to a "show" in North China which would
give the Japanese
military and his own military an opportunity to
blow off their steam but that the basis of final settlement would
be pretty well agreed upon before the fight began and would probably
involve recognition of the Japanese sphere of influence in North
China as well as other concessions.
This program I am quite sure
was under consideration when the Chire se patience begame exhausted,
and they decided instead to come out from under the desk.
HMB: MF
Very sincerely,
+ me
H. M.
Bixby
